channel.title: The San Francisco Standard - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The San Francisco Standard (sfstandard.com)

item.title: The true cost of child care in San Francisco, according to 8 city families
item.description: We asked parents across the income spectrum to open their books and reveal the cost of raising kids in the city.

item.title: For Logan Webb, the Giants’ next era is all about playoff success
item.description: The team’s ace is just as frustrated as fans about finishing around .500, but Webb believes the Tony Vitello era will be different.

item.title: ‘Star Trek: Starfleet Academy’ wants you to flash the Vulcan salute at Pier 39
item.description: Iconic franchise celebrates 60 years and its latest show with various promos across SF.

item.title: How Harrison Bader can transform the Giants’ outfield
item.description: Left fielder Heliot Ramos and right fielder Jung Hoo Lee are excited to see how the former Gold Glove Award winner fits in at Oracle Park.

item.title: Two soba spots, one block apart. We tried both to find SF’s best bowl
item.description: Soba Sora and Sobakatsu both specialize in freshly made buckwheat noodles. But which one is worth the line?

item.title: SF teachers’ strike is over. The real labor battle is just beginning
item.description: Also in Power Play: Some of SF’s richest are going for gubernatorial hopeful Matt Mahan.

item.title: An insider’s guide to Chinatown’s hidden-gem restaurants
item.description: Cynthia Huie of the gift shop On Waverly knows her hood. Here’s where she satisfies her cravings for Chinese American comfort food — or a cocktail.

item.title: The East Bay’s hottest party is a protest on a freeway overpass
item.description: Friday nights on west Berkeley’s I-80 pedestrian bridge now means glow sticks, costumes, and joyful resistance.

item.title: Could Barry Bonds thrive on TV? There’s only one way to find out.
item.description: Netflix is reportedly courting the home-run king for its Opening Day coverage, but Bonds has never looked entirely comfortable in front of the camera.

item.title: There might be snow on Bay Area peaks Tuesday morning
item.description: San Francisco may record two inches of rain, while rounds of additional storms could cause snow accumulations on the region’s highest mountains.
